title: Hydraulics & Energy Management

competencies.text: Investigate how pressure is transmitted in fluids.
Explain how cross-sectional area affects output force. Analyze electricity consumption data and propose energy-efficient practices.

days.title: Pressure and Pascal's Principle
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will investigate how pressure is transmitted in fluids, explain how area affects output force, and analyze electricity use to propose energy-saving practices.

💧 Pressure

pressure (P) = force (F) ÷ area (A), unit: pascal (Pa) = 1 N/m²

The same force on a smaller area gives a bigger pressure. A sharp knife cuts better than a dull one; a nail's point goes into wood; wide tires keep a tractor from sinking into mud because they spread the weight over a larger area.

🔬 Pascal's Principle

Pressure applied to a fluid in a closed container is transmitted equally to every part of the fluid and to the container walls. Liquids work best because they are almost incompressible — pushing on them does not squeeze them smaller; the push is passed on.

Try it: squeeze a closed plastic bottle full of water — the push you give at one spot is felt by the whole bottle at once.

🤔 Think about it: Why do you sink into soft sand when you stand on tiptoe but not when you lie flat? Use the idea of area to explain.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: A 600 N box rests on a floor area of 0.2 m². What pressure does it exert?
scenario.explanation: P = F ÷ A = 600 N ÷ 0.2 m² = 3,000 Pa. 120 Pa comes from multiplying; 0.00033 comes from dividing the wrong way.

scenario.text: Why does a sharp knife cut tomatoes more easily than a dull one?

choices.label: The same force acts on a smaller area
A sharp knife is always much heavier
The dull knife has more air pressure
A sharp knife uses less friction heat

scenario.explanation: A thin edge has a tiny area, so the same push gives a much larger pressure, enough to break the tomato skin.

scenario.text: Why are liquids, not gases, used inside hydraulic jacks?
scenario.explanation: A gas would squeeze into a smaller volume instead of passing the push along. A liquid hardly compresses, so the pressure is transmitted fully.

days.title: Hydraulic Systems
days.content:
⚙️ How a Hydraulic System Works

Two pistons are joined by a tube of oil. You push the small piston; the pressure travels through the oil and pushes the large piston. The pressure is the same on both sides:

F₁ ÷ A₁ = F₂ ÷ A₂

📝 Worked Example

A jack has a small piston of 0.002 m² and a large piston of 0.10 m². Pushing with 100 N gives a pressure of 100 ÷ 0.002 = 50,000 Pa. The large piston gets F₂ = 50,000 × 0.10 = 5,000 N — enough to lift a car. The force is multiplied by A₂ ÷ A₁ = 50.

⚖️ The Trade-off

Work is not multiplied. To lift the car 1 cm, the small piston must move 50 cm in total (that is why you pump the jack handle many times).

🛠️ Where You See Hydraulics

  • Car and jeepney brakes
  • Hydraulic jacks in vulcanizing shops
  • Excavators and backhoes
  • Dentist and barber chairs

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its meaning or example. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.why: P = F ÷ A, measured in pascals (N/m²).

match.right: Pressure spreads equally in a closed fluid
match.why: A push on one part of the fluid is felt everywhere in it.

match.right: Where the small effort is applied
match.why: A small force on a small area creates the pressure.

match.right: Same pressure gives a larger force
match.why: Force = pressure × area, so a bigger area gives a bigger force.

match.right: How many times the force grows
match.why: If A₂ is 50 times A₁, the output force is 50 times the input.

match.right: Lifts a car with a small hand force
match.why: It multiplies force using two pistons of different areas.

match.right: Carries pedal pressure to the wheels
match.why: The pedal's pressure reaches all four brakes through the fluid.

match.left: Many pumps of a jack handle
match.right: Input piston moves a long distance
match.why: Work is conserved, so a large force needs a long input distance.

days.title: Reading Electricity Use
days.content:
⚡ Power and Energy

Power (watts, W) is how fast an appliance uses energy. Energy is power × time. Electric companies bill you in kilowatt-hours (kWh):

energy (kWh) = power (kW) × time (h)   (1 kW = 1,000 W)

📝 Worked Example

A 1,500 W flat iron used 2 hours a day: 1.5 kW × 2 h = 3 kWh per day. In 30 days: 90 kWh. At ₱12 per kWh, that costs about ₱1,080 a month.

🧾 Reading Your Bill

Your bill shows the previous and present meter readings; the difference is the kWh you used. Compare months: a sudden jump usually means a new appliance, longer use, or a faulty appliance.

🔍 Big vs Small Users

ApplianceTypical power
Air conditioner800–1,500 W
Flat iron / rice cooker500–1,500 W
Refrigerator100–200 W (runs all day)
Electric fan50–75 W
LED bulb5–10 W

High power and long hours make the biggest bill. A refrigerator has a small wattage, but because it runs 24 hours a day it is often one of the top users in a home.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Compute and decide. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A 1,000 W rice cooker is used 1 hour a day for 30 days. How much energy does it use?
scenario.explanation: 1 kW × 1 h × 30 days = 30 kWh. 30,000 forgets to change watts to kilowatts.

scenario.text: A hydraulic press has a 0.01 m² input piston and a 0.5 m² output piston. You push with 40 N. What output force do you get?
scenario.explanation: The force is multiplied by A₂ ÷ A₁ = 0.5 ÷ 0.01 = 50, so F₂ = 40 × 50 = 2,000 N.

scenario.text: Your family's bill rose by 60 kWh this month. Which new habit is the MOST likely cause?

choices.label: Using a 1,000 W heater 2 hours a day
Charging one phone fully every single night
Leaving a 5 W LED bulb on all night long
Using a 60 W fan for 1 hour a day

scenario.explanation: 1 kW × 2 h × 30 days = 60 kWh. The phone (about 0.3 kWh/month), the LED (about 1.5 kWh) and the fan (1.8 kWh) are far too small.

scenario.text: Two refrigerators keep food equally cold. Model A uses 1.2 kWh a day; Model B uses 0.8 kWh a day. At ₱12/kWh, about how much does Model B save in a year?
An excavator arm uses oil, not air, to move its heavy bucket. Which reason is BEST?

choices.label: Oil passes the pressure on without compressing
Oil is much cheaper than air in every country
Air would make the metal arm too heavy to lift
Oil keeps the steel arm from rusting too quickly

scenario.explanation: Air would compress like a spring and the arm would bounce or sag. Oil is nearly incompressible, so it transmits the pressure fully and smoothly.

days.title: Saving Energy Wisely
days.content:
🌱 Why Save Energy?

Most Philippine electricity comes from coal, natural gas and geothermal plants. Using less energy lowers the bill, reduces carbon emissions and eases the load on the grid during hot months when brownouts happen.

📊 Analyze Before You Act

  1. List each appliance, its power and hours of use per day.
  2. Compute kWh per month for each one.
  3. Target the biggest users first — saving 10% on the aircon beats switching off one LED bulb.

✅ Practices That Work

  • Switch to LED bulbs (about 85% less energy than incandescent for the same light).
  • Choose appliances with a higher Energy Efficiency Factor on the yellow energy label; inverter aircons and refrigerators save the most.
  • Set the aircon to 24–25 °C and clean its filter.
  • Unplug chargers and TVs — standby power adds up.
  • Iron clothes in one batch instead of a few pieces every day.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What is the SI unit of pressure?
escape.explanation: Pressure is force per area: 1 pascal = 1 newton per square meter. Newtons measure force, joules energy and watts power.

escape.text: In a hydraulic lift, what happens when the output piston is 20 times larger in area than the input piston?

choices.label: The output force is 20 times larger
The output force is 20 times smaller
The output piston moves 20 times farther
The pressure on the output is 20 times larger

escape.explanation: The pressure is the same everywhere in the fluid, so the force grows with the area: F₂ = 20 × F₁. The output piston moves 20 times LESS.

escape.text: A 100 W bulb is left on 10 hours a day. How much energy does it use per day?
escape.explanation: 0.1 kW × 10 h = 1 kWh. 1,000 forgets to convert watts to kilowatts.

escape.text: A household wants to cut its bill the MOST. Its aircon runs 8 h/day; it also has 6 LED bulbs. What should it do FIRST?

choices.label: Raise the aircon setting and clean its filter
Replace all the LED bulbs with newer LED bulbs
Unplug the electric fan during the daytime hours
Turn off the LED bulbs one hour earlier each night

escape.explanation: The aircon is the biggest user (about 1 kW × 8 h = 8 kWh/day); small savings there beat anything done with tiny LED bulbs.

escape.text: Which is NOT an application of Pascal's principle?

choices.label: A solar panel charging a battery
A barber chair raised by a pump

escape.explanation: Brakes, jacks and pump chairs move force through a liquid under pressure. A solar panel turns light into electricity — no fluid pressure involved.

escape.text: Two aircon units cool a room equally. Which label information tells you which is CHEAPER to run?

choices.label: The bigger and heavier outdoor unit

escape.explanation: The Energy Efficiency Factor on the yellow label compares cooling output to electricity used; a higher value means lower running cost.
